record.original_question: Let I_n = {0, 1/n, 2/n, ..., 1}. Given any discrete t-norm T on I_n, extend it to a t-norm T* on [0, 1] by setting T*(x, y) = min(x, y) when max{x, y} = 1 and otherwise T*(x, y) = T(floor(nx)/n, floor(ny)/n). Let tau*_n be the set of all such extensions of all discrete t-norms on I_n, and let tau* be the union of tau*_n over all positive integers n. What is the closure of tau* in the norm of uniform convergence? In particular, does that closure contain all strict t-norms, all continuous t-norms, and all t-norms?

evidence.quote: Given a discrete t-norm T on the set I_n = {0, 1/n, 2/n, ..., 1}, one can extend it to a t-norm on [0, 1] by a piecewise constant extension.
Denote tau*_n the set of all such extensions of all discrete t-norms on I_n and put tau* = union over n in N of tau*_n.

Problem 4.1. What is the closure of the set tau* with respect to the norm of uniform convergence? In particular, are the sets of all strict t-norms, of all continuous t-norms and of all t-norms inside?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A triangular norm (t-norm) is a binary operation T : [0,1]^2 → [0,1] that is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and satisfies T(x,1) = x for every x ∈ [0,1]. A t-norm T is called continuous if it is continuous as a function on [0,1]^2, and strict if it is continuous, strictly increasing on (0,1]^2, and Archimedean (i.e., for all x ∈ (0,1) there exists n with T(x, x, …, x) (n times) < x for n large enough — equivalently, T is isomorphic to a t-norm with generator giving strict monotonicity). For a positive integer n, let I_n = {0, 1/n, 2/n, …, 1}. A discrete t-norm on I_n is an operation T : I_n × I_n → I_n that is commutative, associative, non-decreasing in each argument, and has 1 as neutral element.

Given a discrete t-norm T on I_n, define its piecewise-constant extension T* : [0,1]^2 → [0,1] by
  T*(x, y) = min(x, y) if max(x, y) = 1,
  T*(x, y) = T(⌊nx⌋/n, ⌊ny⌋/n) otherwise.
Then T* is a t-norm on [0,1]. Let τ*_n denote the set of all such extensions T* of all discrete t-norms T on I_n, and set
  τ* = ⋃_{n ∈ ℕ} τ*_n.

Equip the set of all t-norms with the metric induced by the uniform norm ||·||_∞ on functions [0,1]^2 → [0,1]. Determine the closure cl(τ*) of τ* with respect to uniform convergence. In particular, decide whether cl(τ*) contains:
(a) every strict t-norm on [0,1];
(b) every continuous t-norm on [0,1];
(c) every t-norm on [0,1].
